title: Group: legal entity register and organization charts
source_system: Corporate secretary's entity management system; group HR organization charts
what_it_shows: A publicly traded holding company (SEC registrant) with three subsidiaries: Cris Santos College, LLC; Cris Santos Learning Technologies, Inc.; and Cris Santos Student Health, LLC (acquired 2024). Corporate shared services (identity, network, security operations, cloud and data platform, HR, finance, legal, internal audit) sit in the parent. Organization charts show the Group CISO, Group Chief Risk Officer, Group Chief Privacy Officer, Group General Counsel, the College CISO, the Education Software CISO, the Student Health security and compliance lead, and group internal audit reporting to the board audit committee

title: Group: HR roster by division
source_system: Group HR system (HR SaaS)
what_it_shows: 45,000 employees: Higher Education about 25,000 (faculty and staff), Education Software about 8,500, Student Health about 6,500, corporate shared services about 5,000. Termination events feed SYS-G1 identity governance

title: Group: FY2025 revenue by division
source_system: ERP general ledger; FY2025 Form 10-K segment note
what_it_shows: Revenue of about $18.0 billion: Higher Education about $9.6 billion, Education Software about $5.8 billion, Student Health about $2.6 billion

title: Group: intercompany service agreement for the college's Campus Platform tenant (2021)
source_system: Group legal contract management system
what_it_shows: The 2021 agreement between Cris Santos College and Education Software covers hosting of the college's SIS and LMS tenant with student financials on the Campus Platform, service levels and charges. It has no safeguards schedule, no incident notice term, no right-to-assess clause, and no FERPA direct-control or redisclosure terms. It does not state how security duties are split between the college and Education Software

title: Group: intercompany BAA and clinic services agreement (2024)
source_system: Group legal contract management system; data request tickets
what_it_shows: An intercompany BAA between corporate shared services and Student Health, signed 2024. A clinic services agreement between the college and Student Health, signed 2024, with school-official terms for the 22 campus clinics and an exchange of enrollment status and immunization compliance status. Other data requests between the college and Student Health are handled by ticket; no written data-sharing standard or approval step covers them

title: Group: SYS-G1 authentication and sign-in policy export
source_system: Group identity platform admin console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: About 41,000 federated workforce users. MFA required for every federated user, by push approval for workforce users and phishing-resistant hardware keys for administrators; lockout after 10 failed attempts; passwords checked for length and against a banned-password list; identifiers assigned from HR and SIS records and never reused. Conditional access requires MFA and a compliant device for remote access; there is no VPN. Higher Education and Education Software users are fully federated; about 60% of Student Health users are federated

title: Group: SYS-G1 identity governance export
source_system: Identity governance module (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Joiner-mover-leaver workflows driven by HR events for all federated divisions; SRLP roles requested in identity governance and approved by the data owner; quarterly certification campaigns; workforce accounts inactive for 60 days disabled by a scheduled job (job log on file); temporary and contractor accounts carry an end date and expire automatically, as a listing of 20 contractor accounts shows; account events forwarded to the SIEM. Student Health legacy domain (SYS-S2) accounts are not in identity governance

title: Group: privileged access management inventory and policy
source_system: Privileged access management console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Administrators hold separate privileged accounts. Privileged roles for corporate, Higher Education and Education Software administrators are granted just in time with approval and session recording. Vendor maintenance sessions on hub and warehouse components are brokered through PAM; production changes to the hub and warehouse need PAM elevation; pipelines deploy with dedicated identities. 9 named college administrators hold the SIS tenant administrator role

title: Group: Q1 2026 access certification results
source_system: Identity governance module (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Quarterly certification completed for federated division applications, SRLP privileged roles and warehouse roles, which data owners certified. Separation-of-duties rules between FAMS awarding and student financials disbursement were checked in the campaign

title: Group: endpoint configuration baseline and EDR coverage report
source_system: Endpoint management console; EDR console (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: Managed endpoints lock after 10 minutes idle; managed laptops and tablets have disk encryption on. EDR runs on managed endpoints, servers and cloud hosts, including integration hub compute, campus servers, clinic servers and the 12 SAIG workstations. Returned endpoints are wiped under NIST SP 800-88, with wipe records on file

title: Group: SIEM data source inventory, detection rules and analytics
source_system: Group SIEM (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: 24x7 SOC. Identity, cloud, PAM, endpoint, integration hub and warehouse query logs and SIS tenant audit records (exported hourly) are onboarded and correlated, with case automation. The event catalog includes sign-ins, role changes, SIS record views and exports, aid and bank detail changes, warehouse queries and integration job runs. Rules cover bulk SIS exports, aid and bank detail changes and unusual sign-ins; behavior analytics cover interactive workforce sign-ins. No rule covers integration hub service accounts or support console sessions, and egress volume rules do not include warehouse object storage exports

title: Group: log archive, retention and logging go-live settings
source_system: Central log archive account (SYS-G3); SIEM retention settings; go-live checklist
what_it_shows: Logs are written to a separate write-once archive account that only SOC roles can read; retention is 1 year online and 6 years archived. Use of privileged functions in PAM, the cloud consoles and the SIS tenant administrator role is retained in the SIEM. The go-live checklist requires logging to be confirmed for each new interface

title: Group: SOC case export and runbooks, April 2025 to March 2026
source_system: Group case management system (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: Incidents are tracked in one case system with timelines, evidence, group playbooks and post-incident reports; a liaison is named for each division; the college liaison joins incidents that touch the SRLP

title: Group: vulnerability scan and patch compliance reports, January to March 2026
source_system: Vulnerability scanner; patch management console (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: Monthly authenticated scans of the integration hub and warehouse, with results sent to remediation tickets; critical findings on hub and warehouse components patched within 15 days; the Campus Platform is scanned by Education Software. Servers at the 6 legacy campuses are patched by campus IT, and their patch reports are kept separately

title: Group: 2026-03 penetration test report and scope letter
source_system: Group security testing program records
what_it_shows: An independent penetration test of the college's Campus Platform tenant and the student portals was completed in 2026-03. The scope letter does not list the integration hub, the student data warehouse or the 6 legacy campuses

title: Group: incident response plan, notification matrix, exercise reports and responder training
source_system: Group policy repository; SOC exercise library; training records
what_it_shows: The group incident response plan and POL-03 (2025) assign roles and FSA and FTC notice steps. The notification matrix lists FSA, the FTC, HIPAA, customer contracts, state law and the SEC. Exercise reports for 2025 and 2026 show technical playbooks tested each quarter; none covered notifications across divisions. Incident responders and division liaisons train each year; the college's financial aid and registrar liaisons were trained in 2026-04

title: Group: policy library, program plan and standards
source_system: Group policy repository
what_it_shows: The group information security program plan and group policies POL-01 to POL-05 (2025), aligned to CSF 2.0, with group standards for logging, configuration management, cloud guardrails, contingency planning, awareness training, personnel security, data classification, risk assessment, control assessment and continuous monitoring. Division documents on file: the Higher Education supplement, the Education Software supplement v2025 (aligned 2025-10), and the Student Health standards (2023)

title: Group: common control catalog and inheritance matrices
source_system: Group GRC tool
what_it_shows: The common control catalog lists 98 corporate controls with their providers and owners. Inheritance is documented in the Higher Education inheritance matrix (2025) and, for Education Software, in its SOC 2 system description, where group services are carved in. No inheritance matrix for Student Health was provided

title: Group: risk management strategy, 2025 risk registers and quarterly risk reports
source_system: Group GRC tool
what_it_shows: The risk strategy sets acceptance authority: Very Low and Low by the division security and compliance lead; Moderate by the division president; High by the Group Chief Risk Officer with the Group CISO, reported to the board risk committee; Very High by the board risk committee only. 2025 group and division registers are on file with a change log; division risks roll into the group register each quarter, and a quarterly risk report goes to the board risk committee

title: Group: board risk committee and audit committee minutes, 2025 to 2026-Q1
source_system: Corporate secretary's board portal
what_it_shows: The board risk committee receives quarterly cyber and risk reports; the board audit committee oversees group internal audit

title: Group: FY2025 Form 10-K cybersecurity disclosure and disclosure committee charter
source_system: SEC filings; disclosure committee records
what_it_shows: The FY2025 Form 10-K includes the Reg S-K Item 106 cybersecurity disclosure. The disclosure committee charter gives the committee the Form 8-K Item 1.05 materiality decision; an Education Software liaison sits on the committee

title: Group: internal audit charter and 2026 audit plan
source_system: Group internal audit
what_it_shows: Internal audit reports to the board audit committee, and its assessors do not operate the controls they test. The 2026 plan assesses group common controls once and samples division controls, including a first sample of Student Health

title: Group: cloud account, IAM and resource inventory, providers A and B
source_system: Cloud consoles; group asset inventory (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Provider A hosts the corporate landing zone, the group data platform with the college integration hub and student data warehouse, and division corporate workloads. Provider B hosts the Campus Platform (SYS-E1), the District Platform (SYS-E2), the support console and release pipeline (SYS-E3), the group backup vault and the data platform disaster recovery replica, which includes the warehouse. The integration hub runs in one region with no standby. Cloud IAM roles are federated from SYS-G1 with no long-lived cloud users; resources are inventoried automatically across division accounts

title: Group: guardrail compliance, infrastructure code and network policy exports
source_system: Guardrail policy service; infrastructure code repository; hub firewall management (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Guardrails enforce encryption at rest and in transit, logging, approved regions and no public storage in every division account; service allow lists per account type; hub and warehouse baselines defined in infrastructure code. Hub-and-spoke network with deny-by-default rules between spokes, allow lists per interface and a rule review record; the integration hub and warehouse have private endpoints only and no public endpoints. Web application firewall and provider DDoS protection in front of portals; encrypted private links between providers and from campus and clinic cores

title: Group: key management inventory, storage encryption settings and provider cryptography documentation
source_system: Key management service (SYS-G3); provider documentation
what_it_shows: Customer-managed keys per division account, including the hub and warehouse, rotated each year; hub and warehouse storage encrypted with group keys; provider hardware security modules and FIPS-validated cryptographic modules documented by the providers

title: Group: backup vault configuration and backup and restore reports, January to March 2026
source_system: Backup service and vault (provider B)
what_it_shows: Daily backups of provider A workloads, including the integration hub and warehouse, to a vault-locked immutable vault in provider B under a separate backup identity; sample data sets restored each quarter (restore test log)

title: Group: TLS scan of SRLP and portal endpoints
source_system: TLS scanning tool (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: SRLP, portal and integration hub private endpoints accept TLS 1.2 or higher only

title: Group: cloud provider SOC 2 reports and shared responsibility documentation
source_system: Provider compliance portals (providers A and B)
what_it_shows: SOC 2 Type 2 reports for providers A and B covering data center physical access, media sanitization and the infrastructure services in use; the providers' published shared responsibility descriptions

title: Group: training, phishing simulation and acknowledgment records
source_system: Group learning management system (Group HR)
what_it_shows: Annual security awareness and FERPA course for all workforce members, with insider threat content; completion 97%. Quarterly phishing simulations, including fake ISIR correction and verification-document lures sent to financial aid staff. Role-based modules for financial aid, registrar and IT administrators; none assigned to warehouse analysts or integration engineers. Annual acceptable use acknowledgments recorded. Security staff training plans and monthly threat intelligence briefings recorded

title: Group: personnel screening, termination, contractor and sanctions records
source_system: Group HR system; identity governance (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Background checks completed before hire for staff with access to student financial data; federated accounts disabled within 4 hours of the HR termination event; contractors (adjunct staffing agency, integration consultants) sign confidentiality and FERPA terms and are sponsored by a college manager; sanctions log entries recorded under POL-01

title: Group: vendor master and third-party risk records
source_system: Accounts payable vendor master; third-party risk tool
what_it_shows: Active suppliers include cloud providers A and B; the identity, SIEM and EDR vendors; the FAMS, admissions CRM, proctoring, mass notification and transcript clearinghouse vendors; the disbursement bank; the clinic EHR vendor, AI scribe vendor, billing clearinghouse, e-prescribing network and reference lab; the model provider for the AI tutor; enterprise AI assistant and coding assistant vendors; the ERP, HR and payroll providers; the adjunct staffing agency; and a forensic retainer firm. Tier 1 vendors are assessed before contract and each year under the supply chain risk management plan, and vendors and offshore contractors are screened under 28 CFR Part 202. The Campus Platform is billed to the college as an intercompany charge and is not in the vendor master

title: Group: AI tool discovery
source_system: Procurement records; SaaS discovery; SYS-G1 app list; model registries
what_it_shows: AI in use: the admissions CRM applicant scoring feature (since 2025); the college student-success model on the warehouse, shown to advisors through the Campus Platform analytics module; proctoring AI flags and identity verification; the K-12 AI tutoring assistant (pilot since 2026-01); District Platform early warning indicators; the Campus Platform student-success analytics module; the AI scribe pilot at campus clinics; decision support tools in the clinic EHR; a coding assistant for Education Software engineers; and an enterprise generative AI assistant pilot. A counseling triage chatbot is proposed. Workforce use of public generative AI tools was not established

title: Group: records schedules and warehouse retention settings
source_system: College records management; warehouse configuration (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: The college records schedule sets retention for SIS and FAMS records, and the registrar and financial aid review it each year (2026 review record). The warehouse keeps full copies of SIS and aid extracts with no expiry set

title: Group: contract, funding and payment scope checks
source_system: Group contract register; grants records; payment architecture documents
what_it_shows: No federal research contracts or CUI designations in the contract register; no E-Rate funding in any division; no federally assisted substance use disorder program; tuition card payments use a hosted payment page and clinic copays use point-to-point encrypted terminals

title: Group: cyber insurance policy schedule
source_system: Group risk management (insurance) files
what_it_shows: A group cyber insurance policy covering all three divisions is in force for 2026

title: Higher Education: Program Participation Agreement and SAIG Enrollment Agreement
source_system: College regulatory affairs files
what_it_shows: One Program Participation Agreement for the college, in which the college agreed to comply with 16 CFR Part 314; a SAIG Enrollment Agreement; SAIG transmissions run from 12 dedicated workstations at the central financial aid office; the college receives Department of Education program funds

title: Higher Education: consumer and aid recipient counts
source_system: FAMS (SYS-H2) and student financials (SYS-H1) reports
what_it_shows: Customer information is held on about 1.4 million consumers (current and former aid recipients within the record retention period, plus parent borrowers); about 290,000 current aid recipients

title: Higher Education: enrollment and student record counts, 2025-26
source_system: SIS reporting (SYS-H1); institutional research
what_it_shows: About 410,000 students enrolled in the year: about 115,000 on campus or hybrid at 22 campuses in 8 southeastern states and about 295,000 fully online. Online students live in all 50 states, including Colorado and California. No enrolled student is under 13. The college tenant holds about 2.3 million current and former student records

title: Higher Education: FY2025 Title IV compliance audit report
source_system: College finance office
what_it_shows: The independent compliance audit for fiscal 2025 tested GLBA procedures as FSA requires and reported no GLBA finding

title: Higher Education: Qualified Individual designation, college WISP and board reports
source_system: College CISO files; college board of trustees minutes
what_it_shows: Written designation of the College CISO as Qualified Individual (2023), a college employee who reports to the Group CISO. The college WISP (updated 2025) references the group program plan. Written 314.4(i) reports went to the college board of trustees in 2024 and 2025 (board minutes). The 2025 report covers program status and compliance, risk assessment, testing and security events; it does not discuss arrangements with Education Software or Student Health

title: Higher Education: vendor review file and contract clause review
source_system: College CISO vendor files; vendor contracts
what_it_shows: SOC 2 reviews each year are on file for the FAMS, admissions CRM and proctoring vendors. Their contracts carry safeguards and FERPA school-official terms, and the FAMS contract sets 72-hour incident notice. No assessment or SOC 2 review record exists for the Campus Platform, which the college has used since 2021

title: Higher Education: SIS tenant role report, role matrix and SRLP access runbook
source_system: SIS tenant admin console (SYS-H1)
what_it_shows: SIS and LMS roles by function (registrar, financial aid, student accounts, advisor, faculty, student); faculty see their course sections and advisors their assigned students; about 1,900 admissions and enrollment staff see every student's full record, including account holds. Student accounts are created on admission and disabled 2 terms after the last enrollment. The SRLP access runbook is kept by the college identity and access team

title: Higher Education: SIS and LMS tenant settings export
source_system: SIS tenant admin console (SYS-H1)
what_it_shows: MFA required for all workforce users and, since 2025, for all students (student MFA enrollment report); sessions end after 30 minutes idle for workforce users and 60 minutes for students; the sign-in page shows the acceptable use and FERPA notice banner; sample platform audit records carry user, tenant, record, action, time and source address and are exported to the SIEM hourly. Bank detail changes in student financials need a fresh MFA challenge and an out-of-band confirmation; student financials are reconciled daily to FAMS awards. Tenant settings are exported monthly and compared to the approved baseline

title: Higher Education: college change board records, January to March 2026
source_system: College change management system
what_it_shows: Changes to tenant configuration, integrations and warehouse schemas are recorded through the college change board; the change template has a security and privacy impact section; platform releases follow Education Software's release process

title: Higher Education: privacy monitoring review records, January to March 2026
source_system: College privacy office
what_it_shows: The college privacy team reviews monthly reports of bulk exports and record views by admissions and advisor roles; support console access to the college tenant does not appear in the reports

title: Higher Education: FAMS user report and audit log settings
source_system: FAMS admin console (SYS-H2)
what_it_shows: College staff sign in through SSO with MFA; vendor support accounts are local to the FAMS; FAFSA data in the FAMS is limited to financial aid roles; the vendor generates audit logs that the college can export; no college review record of the logs was provided

title: Higher Education: SAIG workstations and central financial aid office access
source_system: Endpoint inventory; badge access system
what_it_shows: 12 dedicated SAIG workstations in a badge-controlled room, with EDR and application allow listing; 4 pre-imaged spare workstations; badge logs for the room

title: Higher Education: legacy campus network and server documentation (6 campuses acquired in 2023)
source_system: Campus IT network diagrams and server inventories (SYS-H4)
what_it_shows: Flat networks at the 6 campuses, with the legacy SIS and file servers on the campus user segment; servers are administered with local administrator accounts; about 340 staff sign in to the legacy SIS with local accounts without MFA; file servers hold scanned aid documents with no encryption at rest configured; the legacy SIS loads into the integration hub nightly; migration to the SIS tenant is planned by 2027-06-30

title: Higher Education: admissions CRM configuration and applicant scoring feature
source_system: Admissions CRM admin console (SYS-H3); vendor documentation
what_it_shows: The vendor's applicant scoring feature has been enabled since 2025 and scored about 380,000 applications in the 2025-26 cycle. Inputs include inquiry and application data, prior education, age, home ZIP code and a financial aid interest flag; low-band applicants receive automated email only. No bias test results, applicant notice or review against Colorado SB26-189 were found in the documents provided. Applicant aid estimates are stored in the CRM

title: Higher Education: proctoring service configuration
source_system: Proctoring vendor admin console (SYS-H5)
what_it_shows: Identity verification by face matching and AI flags with timestamps; biometric and video retention set to 1 term; flags go to faculty, and no written flag review rule is on file

title: Higher Education: FERPA annual notice, disclosure log and records request log
source_system: Registrar records
what_it_shows: The fall 2025 annual notice states school official criteria and does not name contractors such as Education Software, Student Health or AI vendors. A manual disclosure log covers registrar disclosures; automated disclosures to the transcript clearinghouse and the proctoring vendor are not recorded per student. Inspection requests in 2025-26 closed in a median of 9 days. Electronic consent forms are in the student portal; an emergency disclosure procedure is on file with 2025 records

title: Higher Education: campus safety systems inventory
source_system: College campus safety office records
owner: College vice president of campus safety
what_it_shows: Mass notification SaaS from one vendor, access control servers on campus networks, and CCTV at 22 campuses; the notification service has its own sign-in for break-glass use

title: SRLP: student data warehouse grants export, data catalog and data set register
source_system: Warehouse database and catalog (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Access is by schema role, and analyst roles can query all student schemas; data owners certify warehouse roles each quarter. 64% of tables carry a data owner and data type tag; no purpose field is populated. FAFSA-derived fields from FAMS sit in tables open to analyst roles and feed the student-success model. The data set register records the legal authority for SIS and FAMS data sets

title: SRLP: integration hub interface catalog, flow definitions and architecture
source_system: Integration hub (SYS-G3); SRLP architecture document
what_it_shows: Interfaces are defined, with technical specifications, for SIS to FAMS, CRM to SIS, LMS to warehouse, proctoring, legacy campus SIS nightly loads, and the two-way enrollment and immunization exchange with the clinic EHR (SYS-S1); 14 service accounts run the integrations. The architecture document shows tenant, integration and analytics layers connected by private endpoints

title: SRLP: integration hub secret inventory
source_system: Cloud secret store (provider A)
what_it_shows: The 14 integration hub service accounts use static secrets; 5 secrets are older than 1 year; no rotation date is recorded

title: SRLP: contingency plan, recovery runbook and test records
source_system: College continuity library
what_it_shows: The SRLP contingency plan (2026) covers loss of the Campus Platform, the integration hub and FAMS, with manual workarounds (printed rosters, check refunds, deadline extensions); the recovery runbook reconciles student financials to FAMS awards before refunds are released. No test record includes the college integration hub, FAMS interfaces or refund reconciliation; a joint SRLP test plan is in draft

title: Education Software: customer register, standard contracts and support runbook
source_system: Contract management system; customer CRM
what_it_shows: About 900 college and university customers and about 5,400 school districts; about 4,100 districts have users under 13. Standard contracts set 72-hour notice of a security incident affecting customer data and state that the customer controls use of its records; the standard college contract includes a safeguards schedule; district contracts authorize collection for the school's educational purpose. About 1,300 district contracts carry state-specific terms with shorter or different notice duties, and no register of those terms exists. The support runbook holds the customer notice procedure. No federal agency customers

title: Education Software: SOC 2 Type 2 report for the period ending 2025-06-30
source_system: Education Software compliance office
what_it_shows: Type 2 report (Security, Availability, Confidentiality) on both platforms for 2024-07-01 to 2025-06-30, with group identity, SOC and backup services carved in; platform encryption at rest and complementary user entity controls for customers are described

title: Education Software: support console role model and account list
source_system: Support console administration (SYS-E3)
what_it_shows: 61 support accounts hold a role with read access to every customer tenant on SYS-E1 and SYS-E2, including the college's tenant. The role is not tied to a ticket or a time limit. Console access is logged by tenant; the logs are not shared with customers

title: Education Software: trust page, subprocessor list and marketing materials
source_system: Public website and its change history; marketing campaign files
what_it_shows: The trust page states that staff access customer data only with customer permission; the subprocessor list does not name the AI tutor's model provider; tutor marketing calls it safe for every grade

title: Education Software: children's information security program, coordinator designation and online notice
source_system: Education Software compliance office; public website
what_it_shows: A memo dated 2026-02 designates the Education Software CISO as program coordinator. The written children's information security program was adopted in 2026-03, with an annual risk assessment and a first program evaluation scheduled for 2027-03-31. The online notice published in 2026-04 includes the retention policy: district data is deleted 90 days after contract end

title: Education Software: tenant list against contract end dates
source_system: Platform tenant registry (SYS-E2); contract management system
what_it_shows: Data of 212 former district customers is still held after contract end, some of it more than 3 years after contract end; a retention exception report lists them

title: Education Software: AI tutoring assistant release records and pilot configuration
source_system: Release and change records (SYS-E3); District Platform configuration (SYS-E2)
what_it_shows: Pilot launched in 2026-01 in 140 districts for grades 3 to 12 (about 410,000 student users, about 160,000 of them under 13). It uses a hosted large language model from a third-party model provider under a contract with zero-data-retention and no-training terms. The release record shows a security review and no children's privacy review; no district contract updates or subprocessor notices are recorded; 31 of the 140 pilot districts signed their contracts before 2026-01. Prompts and responses are logged by tenant and student pseudonym for 90 days; teachers see conversations in dashboards, and districts can turn the feature off

title: Education Software: platform architecture, identity, isolation and failover records
source_system: Architecture repository; SRE records; capacity dashboards (SYS-E1, SYS-E2)
what_it_shows: Both platforms are multi-tenant in provider B, with tenant keys and row-level policies; isolation tests run with each release; a warm standby region and point-in-time recovery (15 minutes); failover is tested twice a year; capacity dashboards are kept. The Campus Platform holds about 6.5 million college student records, including the college tenant, and the District Platform has about 22 million student users (about 8 million under 13). Students, applicants and families sign in through the platform identity service with MFA options per customer; family accounts in some districts use passwords only

title: Education Software: integration partner and contractor assurance register
source_system: Third-party risk tool
what_it_shows: About 140 integration partners; written security assurances are on file for all but 23. Offshore contractors have no production data access; a QA contractor's request for production data access is pending

title: Education Software: release pipeline, code review and scan records
source_system: Release pipeline and source hosting (SYS-E3)
what_it_shows: Each release has a change approval, automated tests and release notes; code review records exist for platform code and for college-built integration code; the pipeline inventory and dependency and pipeline scan results are kept

title: Education Software: product documentation for early warning indicators and the analytics module
source_system: Product documentation (SYS-E1, SYS-E2); analytics design review
what_it_shows: Documentation for District Platform early warning indicators and the Campus Platform student-success analytics module describes intended uses and is silent on prohibited uses; no developer documentation package for Colorado SB26-189 exists; the 2026 analytics design review shows product analytics use aggregated, de-identified metrics; filtering is described as a customer feature

title: Student Health: acquisition records, clinic site list and patient volumes
source_system: Student Health operations reporting; group corporate development files
what_it_shows: Acquired in 2024. 96 clinic sites: 22 student health and counseling clinics on Cris Santos College campuses, 58 clinics under management contracts for 37 unaffiliated colleges and universities, and 16 community urgent care sites. About 310,000 student patients and about 190,000 nonstudent patients a year. Claims go electronically to health plans through one clearinghouse; the urgent care sites accept Medicaid

title: Student Health: legacy identity domain user report
source_system: Legacy directory (SYS-S2)
owner: Student Health security and compliance lead
what_it_shows: About 40% of Student Health users sign in through the legacy domain; on-site clinical workstations use passwords only; legacy accounts are disabled the next business day after termination; legacy file shares are open to all staff at each site; migration to SYS-G1 is in progress

title: Student Health: division standards (2023)
source_system: Student Health policy library
owner: Student Health security and compliance lead
what_it_shows: Standards written by the clinic operator in 2023, before the 2024 acquisition, and last reviewed in 2023. They allow front desk logins, require nightly backups without a restore test, let clinic managers approve data exports, and do not address common control inheritance or AI use. No alignment record against group policy was provided

title: Student Health: clinic file server backup and encryption reports
source_system: Backup service (SYS-G3); legacy server console (SYS-S2)
owner: Student Health security and compliance lead
what_it_shows: Clinic file servers have been backed up nightly to the group vault since 2026-03, and no restore test is recorded; volume encryption is on for file servers at 9 of 16 legacy sites; the file servers hold clinic forms, scanned intake forms and insurance cards

title: Student Health: clinic EHR configuration, roles and access review records
source_system: Clinic EHR admin console (SYS-S1)
what_it_shows: Vendor-hosted EHR with vendor replication (RPO 15 minutes per contract); role-based access requested by clinic staff and approved by clinic managers; counseling records in a restricted section; the Privacy Officer reviews access reports weekly; no field records whether a record is PHI or a FERPA record or which institution owns a student record; audit logging on and forwarded to the SIEM; intake forms record student status; e-prescribing runs on shared clinic workstations

title: Student Health: BAA register and clinic management contracts
source_system: Student Health contracts folder
what_it_shows: BAAs with the EHR vendor, the AI scribe vendor (no-training terms), the clearinghouse and corporate shared services (intercompany, 2024). 58 management contracts with 37 colleges and universities carry FERPA school-official and redisclosure terms, with incident notice terms that vary by contract. No contracting college has asked for a SOC report

title: Student Health and SRLP: clinic utilization extract review
source_system: Warehouse tables (SYS-G3); change ticket for the extract; clinic EHR interface log (SYS-S1)

The tables hold record numbers, birth years, ZIP codes, visit dates, clinics and diagnosis categories, with no names, for campus clinic students, students of 3 contracting colleges and about 41,000 nonstudent patients. The change ticket shows no data owner or Privacy Officer approval

title: Group: legal memo on the status of clinic records under FERPA and HIPAA
source_system: Group legal
what_it_shows: Records of students seen at the 22 campus clinics are the college's education or treatment records, and records of students seen at the 58 contract clinics are the contracting institutions' records, under FERPA (34 CFR 99.3); both are excluded from PHI. Records of nonstudent patients and of all patients at the 16 community urgent care sites are PHI. Billing records on students are education records. Student Health is a single covered entity

title: Student Health: breach risk assessment file for the clinic utilization extract
source_system: Student Health privacy office
